If the sender restarts, E11 reaps the staging, and re-compression may produce different bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes → the receiver's persisted bitmap becomes silently invalid.\n16\t\n17\t## Solution Options\n18\t\n19\t### Option A: Preserve Staging Files Across Restarts\n20\t\n21\t**Approach:** Amend T4 to allow exceptional preservation of compressed staging files when resume is possible.\n22\t\n23\t#### Mechanism\n24\t\n25\t1. **Staging lifecycle modification:**\n26\t   - Staging files marked with `resumable` flag when created with compression\n27\t   - E11 reaping skips `resumable` staging files\n28\t   - T4 wiping deferred until session expires or explicitly abandoned\n29\t\n30\t2. **Session management:**\n31\t   - Sender tracks active sessions in persistent storage\n32\t   - On startup, sender reunites with preserved staging\n33\t   - User-visible \"abandoned transfers\" UI for cleanup\n34\t\n35\t3. **Privacy compromise:**\n36\t   - Staging persists across browser restarts\n37\t   - Multi-GB files may accumulate on device\n38\t   - T4a partially violated (privacy vs. functionality trade-off)\n39\t\n40\t#### Trade-offs\n41\t\n42\t| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n43\t|-----------|--------|-------|\n44\t| **Privacy (T4)** | ❌ Negative | Staging files persist, violating \"wipe on completion\" requirement |\n45\t| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Preserves compression state → resume works correctly |\n46\t| **Complexity** | ❌ Negative | Requires session tracking, abandonment detection, user cleanup UI |\n47\t| **UX** | ⚠️ Mixed | Resume works, but users manage \"abandoned transfer\" clutter |\n48\t| **Storage** | ❌ Negative | Multi-GB staging files accumulate on device |\n49\t\n50\t#### Implementation Complexity\n51\t\n52\t- **Medium-High** (~300-400 lines)\n53\t  - Modify E11 reaping logic to check `resumable` flag\n54\t  - Add session tracking to beacon protocol\n55\t  - Build user-facing \"abandoned transfers\" management UI\n56\t  - Implement staging expiry TTL (e.g., 7 days)\n57\t  - Add cleanup telemetry and monitoring\n58\t\n59\t#### Risks\n60\t\n61\t1. **Privacy regression:** Staging files persist longer than intended\n62\t2. **Storage exhaustion:** Users accumulate multi-GB files without realizing\n63\t3. **Cross-platform issues:** Staging files may not survive OS cleanup/browser cache clearing\n64\t4. **Edge cases:** Browser crashes, extension updates, OPFS quota limits\n65\t\n66\t---\n67\t\n68\t### Option B: Forbid Resume When Compression is Enabled\n69\t\n70\t**Approach:** Detect compression on the sender, signal via beacon, and fail-fast on resume attempts.\n71\t\n72\t#### Mechanism\n73\t\n74\t1. **Beacon flag protocol:**\n75\t   - `BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled` set when `PacketFlags.Compressed` is set\n76\t   - Receiver reads flag from beacon and suppresses resume UI\n77\t   - No resume state persisted (bitmap not saved to IndexedDB)\n78\t\n79\t2. **StreamId behavior:**\n80\t   - Unchanged: Same file → same streamId regardless of compression\n81\t   - Re-selecting same file after restart → fresh transfer (not a resume)\n82\t   - Different compressed session cannot resume from/to uncompressed session\n83\t\n84\t3. **User communication:**\n85\t   - UI shows \"Resume not available with compression enabled\"\n86\t   - Compression toggle shows trade-off: \"Speed (no resume) vs. Robustness (resume)\"\n87\t\n88\t#### Trade-offs\n89\t\n90\t| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n91\t|-----------|--------|-------|\n92\t| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | No staging persistence → T4 fully preserved |\n93\t| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Explicitly disables unsafe resume → no silent corruption |\n94\t| **Complexity** | ✅ Positive | Minimal code change (~50-100 lines) |\n95\t| **UX** | ⚠️ Mixed | Clear trade-off: speed vs. robustness |\n96\t| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n97\t\n98\t#### Implementation Complexity\n99\t\n100\t- **Low** (~50-100 lines)\n101\t  - Add `BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled` enum value\n102\t  - Set flag in beacon when compression enabled\n103\t  - Check flag in receiver resume UI rendering\n104\t  - Update plan.md §8.3 documentation\n105\t\n106\t#### Risks\n107\t\n108\t1. **User confusion:** Users may not understand why resume is unavailable\n109\t2. **Transfer loss:** Multi-hour transfers restart from beginning on interruption\n110\t3. **Connection dependency:** Compression becomes viable only on stable connections\n111\t\n112\t---\n113\t\n114\t### Option C: Use Deterministic Compression\n115\t\n116\t**Approach:** Replace `CompressionStream` with a deterministic compressor that guarantees reproducible output.\n117\t\n118\t#### Mechanism\n119\t\n120\t1. **Custom WASM compressor:**\n121\t   - Integrate a deterministic gzip/zlib implementation (e.g., zlib-ng)\n122\t   - Fix compression level, strategy, and metadata\n123\t   - Strip timestamp, filename, and other variable fields\n124\t\n125\t2. **Determinism guarantees:**\n126\t   - Same input + same compressor version = identical output\n127\t   - Cross-platform consistency via WASM\n128\t   - Versioned compressor to detect algorithm changes\n129\t\n130\t3. **Fallback mechanism:**\n131\t   - If compressor version mismatch, abort resume\n132\t   - Beacon carries compressor version identifier\n133\t   - Receiver validates version before persisting resume state\n134\t\n135\t#### Trade-offs\n136\t\n137\t| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n138\t|-----------|--------|-------|\n139\t| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | Staging still wiped; no persistence needed |\n140\t| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Deterministic compression → safe resume |\n141\t| **Complexity** | ❌ Negative | High complexity; custom compressor integration |\n142\t| **UX** | ✅ Positive | Resume works with compression (best of both) |\n143\t| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n144\t\n145\t#### Implementation Complexity\n146\t\n147\t- **High** (~800-1200 lines)\n148\t  - Integrate WASM compressor build pipeline\n149\t  - Implement compressor versioning and validation\n150\t  - Add compressor unit tests across platforms\n151\t  - Maintain custom WASM dependency\n152\t  - Handle fallback when compressor unavailable\n153\t\n154\t#### Risks\n155\t\n156\t1. **Maintenance burden:** Custom WASM compressor requires ongoing updates\n157\t2. **Build complexity:** Adds WASM compilation to build pipeline\n158\t3. **Browser compatibility:** WASM support varies (though broadly available)\n159\t4. **Performance:** WASM compressor may be slower than native `CompressionStream`\n160\t5. **Version skew:** Compressor updates invalidate all existing resume states\n161\t\n162\t---\n163\t\n164\t## Trade-off Summary\n165\t\n166\t| Option | Privacy (T4) | Correctness | Complexity | UX | Storage | Total |\n167\t|--------|--------------|-------------|------------|-----|---------|-------|\n168\t| **A: Preserve staging** | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ❌ | 1/5 |\n169\t| **B: Forbid resume** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n170\t| **C: Deterministic compression** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n171\t\n172\t**Key:**\n173\t- ✅ = Positive impact (fully meets requirement)\n174\t- ⚠️ = Mixed impact (trade-off or caveat)\n175\t- ❌ = Negative impact (violates requirement or high cost)\n176\t\n177\t## Recommendation\n178\t\n179\t### Chosen Option: **Option B — Forbid Resume When Compression is Enabled**\n180\t\n181\t**Rationale:**\n182\t\n183\t1. **Privacy preservation (T4 compliance):** No staging persistence → privacy posture unchanged\n184\t2. **Correctness guarantee:** Explicitly disabling unsafe resume prevents silent corruption\n185\t3. **Low implementation complexity:** ~50-100 lines vs. 300-1200 lines for alternatives\n186\t4. **Clear user contract:** Speed vs. robustness trade-off is transparent\n187\t5. **No new maintenance burden:** No custom compressor or session tracking\n188\t\n189\t**Why not Option A (preserve staging)?**\n190\t- Violates T4 privacy requirement (staging must be wiped)\n191\t- Adds significant complexity (session tracking, abandonment UI)\n192\t- Storage exhaustion risk on multi-GB files\n193\t- Cross-platform stability issues remain (staging may not survive OS cleanup)\n194\t\n195\t**Why not Option C (deterministic compression)?**\n196\t- High implementation and maintenance complexity\n197\t- Custom WASM compressor dependency\n198\t- Build pipeline complexity\n199\t- Versioning issues (compressor updates invalidate resume states)\n200\t- `CompressionStream` is fast and well-integrated — replacing it is costly\n201\t\n202\t**Why Option B is acceptable:**\n203\t- Users choose between two valid modes:\n204\t  - **Compression ON:** 3-10× faster transfers, no resume (stable connections)\n205\t  - **Compression OFF:** Slower transfers, resume supported (unstable connections)\n206\t- The  None = 0,\n219\t     Compressed = 1 << 0,\n220\t     ResumeDisabled = 1 << 1,  // NEW\n221\t   }\n222\t   ```\n223\t\n224\t2. **Set flag when compression enabled**\n225\t   ```typescript\n226\t   // Compression/Resume Solution Evaluation (bf-3k90)\n\n**Bead:** `bf-3k90`  \n**Depends on:** `bf-2vke` (investigation)  \n**Related:** `bf-17s0` (umbrella resolution task)\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nBased on investigation findings from `bf-2vke`, the core architectural conflict is:\n\n1. **Resume requires statelessness** — Same file + same streamId must produce identical block hashes\n2. **Compression is non-deterministic** — CompressionStream offers no guarantee of reproducible output\n3. **T4 privacy requirement** — Staging files MUST be wiped on completion/cancel/startup (E11)\n\nWhen compression is enabled, the sender's wire payload is the compressed staging file. If the sender restarts, E11 reaps the staging, and re-compression may produce different bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes → the receiver's persisted bitmap becomes silently invalid.\n\n## Solution Options\n\n### Option A: Preserve Staging Files Across Restarts\n\n**Approach:** Amend T4 to allow exceptional preservation of compressed staging files when resume is possible.\n\n#### Mechanism\n\n1. **Staging lifecycle modification:**\n   - Staging files marked with `resumable` flag when created with compression\n   - E11 reaping skips `resumable` staging files\n   - T4 wiping deferred until session expires or explicitly abandoned\n\n2. **Session management:**\n   - Sender tracks active sessions in persistent storage\n   - On startup, sender reunites with preserved staging\n   - User-visible \"abandoned transfers\" UI for cleanup\n\n3. **Privacy compromise:**\n   - Staging persists across browser restarts\n   - Multi-GB files may accumulate on device\n   - T4a partially violated (privacy vs. functionality trade-off)\n\n#### Trade-offs\n\n| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Privacy (T4)** | ❌ Negative | Staging files persist, violating \"wipe on completion\" requirement |\n| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Preserves compression state → resume works correctly |\n| **Complexity** | ❌ Negative | Requires session tracking, abandonment detection, user cleanup UI |\n| **UX** | ⚠️ Mixed | Resume works, but users manage \"abandoned transfer\" clutter |\n| **Storage** | ❌ Negative | Multi-GB staging files accumulate on device |\n\n#### Implementation Complexity\n\n- **Medium-High** (~300-400 lines)\n  - Modify E11 reaping logic to check `resumable` flag\n  - Add session tracking to beacon protocol\n  - Build user-facing \"abandoned transfers\" management UI\n  - Implement staging expiry TTL (e.g., 7 days)\n  - Add cleanup telemetry and monitoring\n\n#### Risks\n\n1. **Privacy regression:** Staging files persist longer than intended\n2. **Storage exhaustion:** Users accumulate multi-GB files without realizing\n3. **Cross-platform issues:** Staging files may not survive OS cleanup/browser cache clearing\n4. **Edge cases:** Browser crashes, extension updates, OPFS quota limits\n\n---\n\n### Option B: Forbid Resume When Compression is Enabled\n\n**Approach:** Detect compression on the sender, signal via beacon, and fail-fast on resume attempts.\n\n#### Mechanism\n\n1. **Beacon flag protocol:**\n   - `BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled` set when `PacketFlags.Compressed` is set\n   - Receiver reads flag from beacon and suppresses resume UI\n   - No resume state persisted (bitmap not saved to IndexedDB)\n\n2. **StreamId behavior:**\n   - Unchanged: Same file → same streamId regardless of compression\n   - Re-selecting same file after restart → fresh transfer (not a resume)\n   - Different compressed session cannot resume from/to uncompressed session\n\n3. **User communication:**\n   - UI shows \"Resume not available with compression enabled\"\n   - Compression toggle shows trade-off: \"Speed (no resume) vs. Robustness (resume)\"\n\n#### Trade-offs\n\n| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | No staging persistence → T4 fully preserved |\n| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Explicitly disables unsafe resume → no silent corruption |\n| **Complexity** | ✅ Positive | Minimal code change (~50-100 lines) |\n| **UX** | ⚠️ Mixed | Clear trade-off: speed vs. robustness |\n| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n\n#### Implementation Complexity\n\n- **Low** (~50-100 lines)\n  - Add `BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled` enum value\n  - Set flag in beacon when compression enabled\n  - Check flag in receiver resume UI rendering\n  - Update plan.md §8.3 documentation\n\n#### Risks\n\n1. **User confusion:** Users may not understand why resume is unavailable\n2. **Transfer loss:** Multi-hour transfers restart from beginning on interruption\n3. **Connection dependency:** Compression becomes viable only on stable connections\n\n---\n\n### Option C: Use Deterministic Compression\n\n**Approach:** Replace `CompressionStream` with a deterministic compressor that guarantees reproducible output.\n\n#### Mechanism\n\n1. **Custom WASM compressor:**\n   - Integrate a deterministic gzip/zlib implementation (e.g., zlib-ng)\n   - Fix compression level, strategy, and metadata\n   - Strip timestamp, filename, and other variable fields\n\n2. **Determinism guarantees:**\n   - Same input + same compressor version = identical output\n   - Cross-platform consistency via WASM\n   - Versioned compressor to detect algorithm changes\n\n3. **Fallback mechanism:**\n   - If compressor version mismatch, abort resume\n   - Beacon carries compressor version identifier\n   - Receiver validates version before persisting resume state\n\n#### Trade-offs\n\n| Dimension | Impact | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Privacy (T4)** | ✅ Positive | Staging still wiped; no persistence needed |\n| **Correctness** | ✅ Positive | Deterministic compression → safe resume |\n| **Complexity** | ❌ Negative | High complexity; custom compressor integration |\n| **UX** | ✅ Positive | Resume works with compression (best of both) |\n| **Storage** | ✅ Positive | No staging accumulation |\n\n#### Implementation Complexity\n\n- **High** (~800-1200 lines)\n  - Integrate WASM compressor build pipeline\n  - Implement compressor versioning and validation\n  - Add compressor unit tests across platforms\n  - Maintain custom WASM dependency\n  - Handle fallback when compressor unavailable\n\n#### Risks\n\n1. **Maintenance burden:** Custom WASM compressor requires ongoing updates\n2. **Build complexity:** Adds WASM compilation to build pipeline\n3. **Browser compatibility:** WASM support varies (though broadly available)\n4. **Performance:** WASM compressor may be slower than native `CompressionStream`\n5. **Version skew:** Compressor updates invalidate all existing resume states\n\n---\n\n## Trade-off Summary\n\n| Option | Privacy (T4) | Correctness | Complexity | UX | Storage | Total |\n|--------|--------------|-------------|------------|-----|---------|-------|\n| **A: Preserve staging** | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ❌ | 1/5 |\n| **B: Forbid resume** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n| **C: Deterministic compression** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | 4/5 |\n\n**Key:**\n- ✅ = Positive impact (fully meets requirement)\n- ⚠️ = Mixed impact (trade-off or caveat)\n- ❌ = Negative impact (violates requirement or high cost)\n\n## Recommendation\n\n### Chosen Option: **Option B — Forbid Resume When Compression is Enabled**\n\n**Rationale:**\n\n1. **Privacy preservation (T4 compliance):** No staging persistence → privacy posture unchanged\n2. **Correctness guarantee:** Explicitly disabling unsafe resume prevents silent corruption\n3. **Low implementation complexity:** ~50-100 lines vs. 300-1200 lines for alternatives\n4. **Clear user contract:** Speed vs. robustness trade-off is transparent\n5. **No new maintenance burden:** No custom compressor or session tracking\n\n**Why not Option A (preserve staging)?**\n- Violates T4 privacy requirement (staging must be wiped)\n- Adds significant complexity (session tracking, abandonment UI)\n- Storage exhaustion risk on multi-GB files\n- Cross-platform stability issues remain (staging may not survive OS cleanup)\n\n**Why not Option C (deterministic compression)?**\n- High implementation and maintenance complexity\n- Custom WASM compressor dependency\n- Build pipeline complexity\n- Versioning issues (compressor updates invalidate resume states)\n- `CompressionStream` is fast and well-integrated — replacing it is costly\n\n**Why Option B is acceptable:**\n- Users choose between two valid modes:\n  - **Compression ON:** 3-10× faster transfers, no resume (stable connections)\n  - **Compression OFF:** Slower transfers, resume supported (unstable connections)\n- The trade-off is explicit and understandable\n- Implementation is trivial and low-risk\n- Privacy and correctness are fully preserved\n\n## Implementation Outline\n\n### Phase 1: Beacon Protocol (Priority: P0)\n\n1. **Add `ResumeDisabled` flag to beacon**\n   ```typescript\n   // src/core/frame/beacon.ts\n   export enum BeaconFlags {\n     None = 0,\n     Compressed = 1 << 0,\n     ResumeDisabled = 1 << 1,  // NEW\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Set flag when compression enabled**\n   ```typescript\n   // Sender beacon construction\n   if (compressionEnabled) {\n     flags |= BeaconFlags.Compressed | BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled;\n   }\n   ```\n\n3. **Update plan.md §8.3** to document restriction explicitly\n\n### Phase 2: Receiver Resume Logic (Priority: P0)\n\n1. **Check flag before persisting resume state**\n   ```typescript\n   // Receiver beacon handler\n   if ((beacon.flags & BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled) !== 0) {\n     // Do NOT persist bitmap or metadata\n     showResumeDisabledMessage();\n     return;\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Suppress resume UI when flag present**\n   ```typescript\n   // UI rendering\n   const canResume = !isResumeDisabled(beacon.flags) && hasPersistedState();\n   ```\n\n### Phase 3: User Communication (Priority: P1)\n\n1. **Add clear messaging:**\n   - \"Resume is not available when compression is enabled\"\n   - \"To enable resume, disable compression in settings\"\n\n2. **Compression toggle tooltip:**\n   - \"Compression: Faster transfers (3-10×), but cannot resume if interrupted\"\n   - \"No compression: Slower transfers, but can resume from last completed block\"\n\n### Phase 4: Testing (Priority: P0)\n\n1. **Unit tests:**\n   - Test beacon flag setting when compression enabled\n   - Test receiver resume suppression when flag present\n\n2. **Integration tests:**\n   - Compressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI NOT shown\n   - Uncompressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI shown\n   - Beacon flag validation end-to-end\n\n3. **Property tests:**\n   - For any file, compression produces deterministic blocks within ONE session\n   - For any file, re-compression MAY produce different blocks across sessions\n\n### Phase 5: Documentation (Priority: P1)\n\n1. **Update plan.md:**\n   - §8.3: Explicitly document \"Resume unsupported when compression enabled\"\n   - §12 (T4): Confirm staging lifecycle unchanged\n   - §10 (E11): Confirm reaping behavior unchanged\n\n2. **Update user documentation:**\n   - Compression vs. resume trade-off explanation\n   - When to use each mode\n\n## Status\n\n✅ **Decision made:** Option B (Forbid resume when compression is enabled)  \n✅ **Implementation status:** Partially complete\n  - Beacon flags defined in `src/core/frame/beacon.ts`\n  - `isResumeDisabled()` function implemented\n  - Plan.md §8.3 documents the restriction\n⏳ A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, fileSize)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. |\n| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. |\n| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never discard collected blocks. |\n| E10 | **OPFS quota exhausted mid-transfer** | Stop, keep completed blocks, export a partial file plus a manifest of what is missing. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. Also a privacy requirement (§12, T4a). |\n| E12 | **Block reaches rank K but fails its hash** | Discard the whole block, clear its bitmap bit, re-collect. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`; keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost. **The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. |\n| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. |\n| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** and drop decode resolution. |\n| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer, do not silently restart. |\n\n---\n\n## 11. Error taxonomy\n\nEvery distinguishable condition gets a stable code and one user-facing sentence. Defined\nnow, before Phase 5 designs any UI — after that, taxonomies get retrofitted to screens.\n\n**Optical / acquisition** (the stall detector's job, `bf-5vm`):\n\n| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n|---|---|---|\n| `E-NO-SIGNAL` | No decodable tiles at all | \"Point the camera at the sending screen.\" |\n| `E-TOO-FAR` | **camera** px/module < 4 (§2) | \"Move closer — the code is too small to read.\" |\n| `E-TOO-CLOSE` | Symbol exceeds frame, or below min focus | \"Move back a little.\" |\n| `E-BLUR` | Sharpness metric below threshold | \"Hold steady.\" |\n| `E-DARK` | Insufficient exposure | \"Too dark — raise the sender's screen brightness.\" |\n| `E-GLARE` | Saturated region over the code | \"Tilt to avoid the reflection.\" |\n| `E-FOCUS-HUNT` | Focus oscillating | \"Tap the screen to lock focus.\" |\n| `E-ORIENTATION` | Detected capture aspect doesn't match the sender's configured setting (§6.3.2) — e.g. sender is shaping the code for landscape but the receiver is held portrait | \"This app works fine held normally — but if you'd like more margin, match the orientation setting on the sending device, or turn the phone sideways.\" (tip, not a blocker — portrait is fully supported) |\n| `E-SENDER-STALLED` | Identical frames repeating | \"The sending device seems paused.\" |","numLines":100,"startLine":793,"totalLines":1408}}}
